definitions.explanation: A person who runs, especially in an athletic context such as a race or relay.
A player on base in baseball who is attempting to advance around the bases to score a run.

examples.japanese: {走者|そうしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦スタート→スタート：11053_sutaato⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{第|だい}{一|いち}→第一：19377_daiichi⟧{走者|そうしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦バトン→バトン：11274_baton⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}した→渡す：02442_watasu⟧。
examples.english: The first runner passed the baton.

notes:
Compound of {走|そう} (running) and ⟦{者|しゃ}→〜者：04662_sha⟧ (person). Used in formal or sports-commentary contexts. In baseball, this is the standard term for a base runner.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{第|だい}{一|いち}→第一：19377_daiichi⟧{走者|そうしゃ}: first runner (in a relay)
- アンカー{走者|そうしゃ}: anchor runner (final leg of a relay)
- {走者|そうしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{塁|るい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: a runner gets on base
- {走者|そうしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{置|お}く→置く：01092_oku⟧: to have runners on base

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ランナー→ランナー：09483_rannaa⟧: runner — loanword used commonly in both athletics and baseball
- ⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧: athlete, player — broader term for any competitor in sports

USAGE:
In everyday baseball conversation, ⟦ランナー→ランナー：09483_rannaa⟧ is often used interchangeably with {走者|そうしゃ}. The Japanese term {走者|そうしゃ} is preferred in formal sports broadcasting and written commentary.
